MARKET OVERVIEW

1. What is the Current Market Regime?
RISK-ON: normal volatility at 32.7% and broad participation, with 8/8 sectors positive over 1W. The breadth signal is strong; volatility remains in the normal range.

2. Which sectors are leading?
Transportation leads at 1W +17.59% / 1M +11.31%; PGSUS (1W: +21.38% | 1M: +14.88%) — ABOVE TREND and THYAO (1W: +18.40% | 1M: +9.13%) — ABOVE TREND are standouts. Banking follows at +13.11% / +6.35%, led by GARAN (1W: +20.65% | 1M: +20.19%) — ABOVE TREND.

3. Which sectors are lagging?
Retail & Food is weakest on the week at +1.55% and remains down 9.98% over 1M; SOKM (1W: -9.09% | 1M: -18.08%) — BELOW TREND is the sharpest laggard. Energy & Chemicals (+4.76% 1W; -16.04% 1M) and Construction & REIT (+5.09% 1W; -10.91% 1M) also show weak monthly profiles.

STOCK PERFORMANCE

4. Top Performing Stocks?
PGSUS (1W: +21.38% | 1M: +14.88%) — ABOVE TREND; GARAN (1W: +20.65% | 1M: +20.19%) — ABOVE TREND; THYAO (1W: +18.40% | 1M: +9.13%) — ABOVE TREND. FROTO (1W: +14.83% | 1M: +1.67%) — ABOVE TREND and TRALT (1W: +13.81% | 1M: -11.39%) — RECOVERY complete the top five.

5. Worst Performing Stocks?
SOKM (1W: -9.09% | 1M: -18.08%) — BELOW TREND; PETKM (1W: -2.47% | 1M: -19.36%) — BELOW TREND; TUPRS (1W: -2.07% | 1M: -14.24%) — BELOW TREND. TKFEN (1W: -1.83% | 1M: -29.28%) — BELOW TREND and KRDMD (1W: -1.77% | 1M: -12.66%) — BELOW TREND round out the bottom five.

6. Momentum Stocks?
PGSUS (1W: +21.38% | 1M: +14.88%) — ABOVE TREND and GARAN (1W: +20.65% | 1M: +20.19%) — ABOVE TREND lead weekly momentum. THYAO (1W: +18.40% | 1M: +9.13%) — ABOVE TREND also confirms strength across both timeframes.

SECTOR OUTLOOK

7. Banking Sector Outlook?
Banking is a clear leader, up 13.11% over 1W and 6.35% over 1M; GARAN (1W: +20.65% | 1M: +20.19%) — ABOVE TREND and AKBNK (1W: +13.57% | 1M: +4.20%) — ABOVE TREND lead. ISCTR (1W: +10.97% | 1M: +7.81%) — ABOVE TREND, YKBNK (1W: +10.89% | 1M: +8.58%) — ABOVE TREND and TSKB (1W: +13.34% | 1M: +5.24%) — ABOVE TREND confirm broad strength.

8. Industrial Sector Outlook?
Heavy Industry gained 5.45% over 1W but remains down 10.90% over 1M; FROTO (1W: +14.83% | 1M: +1.67%) — ABOVE TREND leads. EREGL (1W: +5.24% | 1M: -12.86%) — RECOVERY and TOASO (1W: +10.21% | 1M: -9.13%) — RECOVERY are bounces, while ASELS (1W: -1.61% | 1M: -4.06%) — BELOW TREND remains weak.

9. Energy & Chemicals Outlook?
The sector rose 4.76% over 1W but is down 16.04% over 1M, leaving gains uneven; TRALT (1W: +13.81% | 1M: -11.39%) — RECOVERY and SASA (1W: +6.00% | 1M: -17.62%) — RECOVERY are short-term rebounds. TUPRS (1W: -2.07% | 1M: -14.24%) — BELOW TREND and PETKM (1W: -2.47% | 1M: -19.36%) — BELOW TREND remain under pressure.

PORTFOLIO STRATEGY

10. Portfolio Recommendation?
Maintain a cautiously pro-risk stance: the normal-volatility, 8/8 positive breadth backdrop supports exposure, with leadership concentrated in transportation and banking. Favor confirmed ABOVE TREND names and keep risk controls tight where 1M performance remains negative.

NEXT WEEK OUTLOOK

11. Stocks to Watch Next Week?
PGSUS (1W: +21.38% | 1M: +14.88%) — ABOVE TREND and GARAN (1W: +20.65% | 1M: +20.19%) — ABOVE TREND are momentum leaders to monitor. FROTO (1W: +14.83% | 1M: +1.67%) — ABOVE TREND, TRALT (1W: +13.81% | 1M: -11.39%) — RECOVERY and MGROS (1W: +12.74% | 1M: -2.39%) — RECOVERY offer contrasting continuation and rebound setups.

12. Sectors to Watch Next Week?
Monitor transportation (+17.59% 1W; +11.31% 1M) and banking (+13.11% 1W; +6.35% 1M) for leadership follow-through. Track retail (+1.55% 1W; -9.98% 1M) for signs of stabilization after broad monthly weakness.

13. Key Levels & Triggers?
No XU100 price levels were provided, so specific support and resistance levels cannot be stated. Watch whether breadth remains broad and volatility stays near its normal 32.7% regime; narrowing participation or a volatility spike would weaken the risk-on signal.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

BIST 50 signals remain RISK-ON, supported by normal volatility and positive 1W returns across all eight sectors. Transportation and banking lead, while retail and energy carry the clearest monthly weakness; continued broad participation is the key condition for maintaining the constructive stance.
